newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank Italy fears metalworker deal - industrialists.
newsitem.headline: Bank Italy fears metalworker deal - industrialists.

text.p: The Bank of Italy has not cut rates because it is worried about the inflationary impact of a proposed government solution to the metalworkers' dispute, said the director general of industrialist group Confindustria.
The government has suggested that management offer 1.7 million workers in the metalworker and engineering sector a monthly pay rise of 200,000 lire per month.
Unions, which had been seeking 230,000 lire, accepted the proposal, but management has stuck to its 139,000 lire offer.
Confindustria's Innocenzo Cipolletta said the Bank of Italy shared businessmen's concern that the suggested deal would have a negative impact on inflation.

"The discount rate has not fallen because the Bank of Italy is frightened that if we sign the (metalworkers') contract along the lines laid out by the government, inflation will rise," Cipolletta told reporters at a press conference.
"If (the bank) did not consider 200,000 lire to be inflationary, perhaps it would have already lowered rates," he added.

Central bank governor Antonio Fazio said on Monday that Italian inflation was falling, but warned that risks remained: "These come from public finance and labour costs and monetary policy has to reflect these things."

A source close to the government told Reuters that government ministers had been confident that the Bank of Italy would cut rates before the New Year. Instead the discount rate has remained unchanged at 7.50 percent.
Negotiations over the renewal of contracts in the metalworkers sector, which expired last June, have dragged on for months.

The metalworkers employers federation, Federmeccanica, met earlier on Tuesday to discuss the situation. It has already rejected the government proposals but has said it was still open to negotiations.

Newspapers have reported that the federation might accept the 200,000 lire per month idea if the period of the contract were extended to 2-1/2 years from the present two years and if the government gave certain incentives to the sector.
Federmeccanica was due to hold a press conference at the end of the meeting. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
